audit.title: Transfer Tokens with Data - Defensive Example
audit.summary: This is a high-quality, agent-runnable CCIP tutorial: one complete, import-included Solidity contract, concrete addresses, chain selectors, gas limits, and a clear setup→deploy→recover→explain arc. Its single biggest strength is code completeness and concrete specifics; its biggest opportunity is retrieval — the page carries zero structured metadata (no JSON-LD, no canonical, no machine-readable date) and its headings are concept-titled rather than phrased as the error/symptom questions developers actually type. Honest verdict: strong content wrapped in a retrieval-weak shell; the fixes are discoverability, not prose.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/error-phrased headings and a short FAQ
recommendations.where: "Reprocessing of failed messages" / end of Explanation
recommendations.issue: headings are concept-titled ("Receiving and processing messages") — miss error-string queries
recommendations.change: add H3s or a mini-FAQ phrased as queries: "Why did my CCIP message fail on the destination chain?", "How do I recover tokens locked by a failed CCIP message?", "What does `MessageFailed` mean?" — each answered in one lead sentence pointing to `retryFailedMessage`.
recommendations.why: devs/agents query by symptom and error name; concept-titled prose loses retrieval it otherwise deserves.

recommendations.title: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with canonical + dateModified
recommendations.issue: 0 JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no machine-readable date despite body "Last Updated: 2025-05-19"
recommendations.change: inject `TechArticle` schema with `headline`, `dateModified: 2025-05-19`, `programmingLanguage: Solidity`, canonical URL, `inLanguage: en`.
recommendations.why: structured metadata and visible freshness raise parse-trust and citation rate for agents.

recommendations.title: Lead sub-sections with the defensive-specific answer
recommendations.issue: "The `sendMessagePayLINK` function is similar to the… tutorial"
recommendations.change: open with the concrete difference first: "This contract raises the destination gas limit to 400,000 to cover error-handling logic," then reference the base tutorial.
recommendations.why: a lifted chunk must stand alone; cross-reference-first leads break in isolation.

recommendations.title: Add a one-sentence canonical definition of defensive coding
recommendations.change: add a crisp liftable line: "Defensive coding in a CCIP receiver means catching processing errors internally so the message never reverts, locking the tokens for later owner recovery instead of losing them."

recommendations.title: Replace opaque link text
recommendations.change: "supported tokens for the Avalanche Fuji lane".

recommendations.title: Trim vague quantifiers
recommendations.where: "ensures that your contract is robust," "significantly higher"
recommendations.issue: vague quantifiers (robust, significant, various, some) flagged
recommendations.change: where possible substitute concrete conditions (e.g. quantify the gas overhead of error handling if measurable); otherwise cut.

antiPatterns: No stale-content risk: body date present (2025-05-19), but not machine-readable.
No keyword stuffing, no marketing fluff, no missing imports — clean.
offPageNotes: Metadata gaps (JSON-LD, canonical, og/date) are site-template level, not authorable in this single page — fix at the docs framework layer.
`llms.txt` is already referenced at page top — good; ensure this URL is listed there.
Head metadata "could not be verified" from the served HTML; CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a definitive metadata read before trusting the absence of og/canonical tags.
